captions.headline: The average resume is missing fifty-two percent of its job's keywords.
captions.subline: Eighty-eight percent of employers say their systems filter qualified candidates. We fix the gap.
captions.caption_linkedin:
Two numbers worth understanding together.

The first is from a Harvard Business School study on hiring automation: 88 percent of employers say their hiring systems filter out qualified candidates who do not precisely match the job description. The second is from screening-behavior research released in 2026: the average unoptimized resume is missing 52 percent of the keywords in the target role's description.

Those two numbers describe the same person. A qualified candidate who never makes it past the first scan, because their CV is written the way they actually talk about their work, not the way the job posting talks about it.

The fix is not magic. It is a structural rewrite of the top of your CV per role, with explicit keywords from the job description baked into language that still sounds like a person who did the work. That work takes about twenty minutes by hand and most of us never do it.

Spark Careers does the matching for you. You pick the role. The system shows you the keywords you are missing and rewrites the relevant sections to include them without inventing experience you do not have.

This is the gap we exist to close.

Five minutes. Free. https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w28-mon-b2c

captions.headline: Leisure and hospitality added seventy thousand jobs in May. Five times the monthly average.
captions.subline: If you run a restaurant, hotel, or service business, this is your hiring season.
captions.caption_linkedin:
Specific data for operators in hospitality, food service, and travel.

The May 2026 BLS jobs report shows leisure and hospitality led every other sector with 70,000 new jobs added. That is roughly five times the 12-month average for the category (about 14,000 per month). The catalyst is partly seasonal and partly World Cup hiring, which is pulling forward demand for hospitality staff in host cities.

For a small operator, that creates two simultaneous problems.

Problem one: every other restaurant and hotel in your area is hiring the same person you are. The applicant pool is real but it is also being competed for harder than at any point in the last 18 months.

Problem two: most small hospitality businesses still run hiring through a clipboard, a personal cell phone, and the assistant manager's memory. That system worked when an applicant trickled in once a week. It breaks when five walk in on the same Saturday.

The operators who are about to win this season are the ones who can reply on day one, track every applicant, and not let anybody fall through the cracks because somebody scribbled a phone number on a receipt.

Spark Careers Enterprise is the workspace for the second problem. Seven days free.

captions.headline: Recruiters scan resumes for seven point four seconds on average.
captions.subline: Make the first five lines do all the work.
captions.caption_facebook:
The data on how recruiters actually read your CV.

Research tracking screening behavior in 2026 finds that recruiters spend an average of 7.4 seconds per resume on a first pass. Not seven minutes. Seven and a half seconds.

In that window, they are looking at three things. The job title at the top. The most recent role and the company name. The skills section, if it is in the standard place.

If those three things do not match the role they are filling, they move to the next CV. The deeper content of your work history (the projects, the impact, the metrics) only gets read if those three early signals pass.

Which means the first five lines of your CV have to do almost all of the work. The headline title. The most recent role positioned to match the next one. A short summary that names the specific outcome the role is asking for.

Spark Careers builds those first five lines for you, tailored to each role you apply to. The rest of your CV stays as it is. https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w28-tue-b2c

captions.headline: Plain DOCX fails ATS parsing four percent of the time. Fancy PDF fails eighteen.
captions.subline: The boring format is the format that gets through.
captions.caption_linkedin:
If you are still sending the beautifully designed PDF resume template you bought on Etsy, here is data worth knowing.

Research on ATS parsing accuracy in 2026 finds that plain DOCX files have a parsing failure rate of about 4 percent. PDF files have a failure rate of 18 percent. Single-column layouts parse correctly 93 percent of the time. Two-column layouts drop to 86 percent.

This is one of those rare cases where the boring choice is the obviously correct one and the visually exciting choice is genuinely costing you interviews.

The gap matters because the parsing failure is silent. The ATS does not tell you it could not read your work history. It just scores you as missing the keywords you actually had, and you never hear back. You revise your CV thinking the content was wrong. The content was fine. The container was unreadable.

The rules that hold up across every parser: one column. One simple font like Calibri or Arial. Standard bullet points. Plain text DOCX. Save the artistic version for your portfolio site.

Spark Careers builds CVs in the format that passes parsers. Five minutes. https://spark.risepointcareers.com/?utm_source=social&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=w28-wed-b2c

captions.headline: The team you build this quarter will outlive the cycle.
captions.subline: Slow the start. Speed the reply. Trust the second instinct.
captions.caption_linkedin:
For the founder reading this at the end of a long week.

The job openings, the hospitality boom, the seasonal hiring wave: all of it is happening at the same time. The temptation in a market like this is either to over-correct (rush a hire to get the seat filled before competitors) or to under-correct (freeze entirely until the noise calms down).

Both are mistakes.

The teams that come out of a hot quarter with people they actually wanted are the teams that kept the process tight even when the temptation was to skip steps. The four habits that hold up across cycles are not new. They are just harder to do when the inbox is full.

Reply on day one. Be honest about what the role actually is. Reference check the offer. Trust the second instinct, not the first.

The team you put together this quarter is the team that will carry you through the next twelve months and beyond. It is worth a little discipline now to get it right.

Keep going.

captions.headline: Two million Americans are long-term unemployed. Staying in the search is the job.
captions.subline: The market is harder, not impossible. Keep going.
captions.caption_linkedin:
A statistic from the May 2026 BLS jobs report that almost nobody talks about.

There are now about 2.0 million Americans who have been jobless for 27 weeks or longer. That number is up about 524,000 from a year ago. Long-term unemployed people now make up 27.5 percent of all unemployed people in the country.

If you are in that 27.5 percent, the most important thing you can hear right now is that you are not alone in it and the explanation is not personal.

The long-term number is up for a reason: the macro market is uneven. Some sectors are hiring aggressively (leisure and hospitality added 70,000 jobs in May), other sectors are still in a low-hire, low-fire holding pattern that pushes the search beyond six months for people in those categories. The data on individual job seekers is consistent: most of the gap is sector mismatch, not effort.

The practical move is not to send more applications. It is to widen the search. Look at adjacent industries where your skills transfer. Frame your experience around capability, not titles. Tailor every application that goes out so it lands.

Spark Careers helps with the framing and the tailoring. The endurance is on you. Keep going. The market is harder, not impossible.
